title: US History Essentials
description: Core events, documents and figures from American history

questions.question: In which year was the Declaration of Independence adopted?
questions.explanation: The Second Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776, announcing the separation of the thirteen colonies from Great Britain.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.explanation: George Washington took office in 1789 as the first president. John Adams was his vice president and became the second president in 1797.

questions.question: What are the first ten amendments to the US Constitution collectively known as?
questions.explanation: The first ten amendments, ratified in 1791, are called the Bill of Rights and protect liberties such as freedom of speech, religion and the press.

questions.question: Which 1803 land deal roughly doubled the size of the United States?
questions.explanation: The Louisiana Purchase of 1803 bought roughly 828,000 square miles of French territory and about doubled the size of the young United States.

questions.question: Between which years was the American Civil War fought?
questions.explanation: The Civil War ran from 1861, when Confederate forces fired on Fort Sumter, to 1865, when Lee surrendered at Appomattox Court House.

questions.question: Which president issued the Emancipation Proclamation?
questions.explanation: Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation, effective January 1, 1863, declaring enslaved people in Confederate-held territory to be free.

questions.question: Which constitutional amendment abolished slavery in the United States?
questions.explanation: The 13th Amendment, ratified in 1865, abolished slavery. The 14th granted citizenship and equal protection, and the 15th addressed voting rights regardless of race.

questions.question: What right did the 19th Amendment, ratified in 1920, secure?
choices: The right of women to vote
The right to a jury trial
questions.explanation: The 19th Amendment barred denying the vote on account of sex, securing women's suffrage nationwide after decades of campaigning.

questions.question: Who delivered the 'I Have a Dream' speech at the 1963 March on Washington?
questions.explanation: Martin Luther King Jr. gave the speech from the steps of the Lincoln Memorial on August 28, 1963, a landmark moment of the civil rights movement.

questions.question: In which year did Apollo 11 land the first humans on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed on July 20, 1969, and Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to walk on the Moon.
